[Species Name]Homebrew

Two or three sentences of flavor: what this species is, where it comes from, and how the world reacts when one walks into a tavern.

A second paragraph on how they live: what they value, what they fear, and why an adventurer of this species leaves home.

Creature Type: [Humanoid]

Size: [Medium (about 5–7 feet tall)]

Speed: [30 feet]

As a [Species Name], you have these special traits.

[Trait Name]. [What it does, in 2024 wording: "You have…", "You can…", "Once you use this trait, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest."]

[Trait Name]. [What it does.]

[Species] Lineage. You are part of a lineage that grants you supernatural abilities. Choose a lineage from the [Species] Lineages table. You gain the level 1 benefit of that lineage. When you reach character levels 3 and 5, you learn a higher-level spell, as shown on the table. You always have that spell prepared. You can cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it that way when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast it using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells (choose when you select the lineage).

Lineage budget: level 1 = a cantrip plus one damage resistance; level 3 = a level 1 spell; level 5 = a level 2 spell. More than that and the species is over budget.

[Character Name] Stat BlockHomebrew

Use this when they show up as an ally, a rival, or the final boss. One sentence on how the DM should run them.

2025 Monster Manual order: AC and Initiative on one line, then HP, then Speed. Ability grid reads Str/Int, Dex/Wis, Con/Cha. Immunities lists damage types, a semicolon, then conditions. Flavor immunities ("magic can't put her to sleep") go in a trait. Damage average = dice × (sides + 1) ÷ 2, plus the modifier, rounded down.

Combat Math

Expected damage, the way the dice really fall. A natural 1 always misses, a natural 20 always hits and is a Critical Hit, and a crit doubles the damage dice but not the modifier.

Attack Roll
Expected damage per turn—
Hit chance (crits included)—
Crit chance—
Average on a hit / on a crit—
Expected per attack—
Saving Throw
Expected total damage—
Chance each target fails—
Average on a failure / success—
Expected per target—

Saving throws have no automatic success on a 20 or failure on a 1 under the 2024 rules; only attack rolls do.
